transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I had an insurance physical recently, and the doctor doing it told me my weight was too low. I don't really agree with that, honestly. To me, I just look lean from being up on ladders and working long days.
Do you think you are at a healthy weight?

I mean, yeah, I do. I know my friends and that doctor from the physical are worried about it, but I really feel like they're just overreacting. I'm still showing up to all my jobs, I'm getting my work done, and I feel fine. So, I don't see the problem.
Do you think you are underweight?

No, I don't. Like I said a minute ago, I really just think I'm lean. I definitely don't look at myself and see someone who is underweight. I'm just carrying the weight that makes sense for how much physical work I do every day. So, no, I don't think I am.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I mean, yeah, I guess I am. I just like keeping things where they are. Like, if the scale goes up even a little bit—say, after a client dinner or eating something heavy with bread—I definitely get tense about it. When that happens, I usually start cutting back the next day just to make sure the extra weight doesn't stick. So, yeah, I do worry about gaining.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?
Not really. I mean, my weight has been pretty steady for a while now. I haven't noticed any big drops recently or anything like that. It's just been staying around the same number.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour?
No, I don't really do that. I pretty much just eat what I need to get through the day, you know? I don't ever sit down and eat a whole lot all at once. I try to keep my portions pretty controlled.
Do you exercise to burn off calories?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, my job is pretty physical—I'm a painter, so I'm up and down ladders and moving gear around all day. That keeps me active. But I don't go out of my way to run or hit the gym just to burn off what I ate. Honestly, by the time I get off work, I'm usually too tired for any extra workouts anyway.
Do you think your friends and the doctor who did your physical have a more accurate view of your weight than you do?

I mean, I know my friends and the doctor who did my physical are worried about my weight. But honestly, I feel like they're just overreacting. I'm still showing up to my jobs every day, climbing ladders, and getting all my work done without any issues. So, I don't really see it the way they do.
Do you think your weight is the same as other people your height and age?

I guess I'm probably a bit lighter than most guys my age and height. I mean, I see other guys on the job site and I know I'm definitely on the thinner side compared to them. But I don't really know exactly what they weigh, so it's hard to say for sure. I just know what feels right for me.
Do you think you look underweight when you see yourself in the mirror?

Not really. I mean... when I look in the mirror, I don't see someone who's underweight. I just see myself. I know I'm lean, but to me, I just look normal. I don't look at my reflection and think there's a problem or that I look sick or anything like that.
Have you had a menstrual period in the last few months?
Uh, well... I'm a guy, so no, I don't get menstrual periods.
Does your fear of gaining weight influence what or how much you eat?

Yeah, it definitely does. If I step on the scale and it goes up even a little bit—like maybe after a dinner with a client or if I had something with bread—I get pretty tense about it. So, I'll usually start cutting back on what I eat the next day just to make sure the weight doesn't stick.
Does your fear of gaining weight make you avoid certain foods?

Yeah, it does. I avoid a lot of things, actually. Most days I just keep it to coffee, and maybe a protein bar between paint jobs. Then I'll just have a really small dinner. I just feel like... well, eating a full meal feels like it would slow me down too much, so I just stick to that routine.
Do you limit the types of food you eat to avoid gaining weight?

I mean, I guess I kind of just answered that. I don't really have specific types of food that I completely ban or anything. It's more just... I stick to the routine I just mentioned with the protein bars and keeping the dinner small so the weight stays off.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is what mainly controls how much you eat?

I don't know if I'd say it controls me. I'm not really sure. I mean, like I said, I definitely keep my meals small so I don't put on pounds... but it's also just what I'm used to doing while I'm working. So I don't know if it's mainly the fear, or if it's just my habit at this point. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is the main reason you eat so little?

I mean, maybe it is a bigger reason than I realize. Like... if I have to go to a client dinner or something, or if I eat something heavier like bread, and I see the scale go up even just a little bit the next morning... I get pretty tense about it. Then I'll immediately start cutting back the next day just to make sure the weight doesn't stick. So, yeah, I guess that does mean the fear is driving a lot of it.
Do you think the fear of gaining weight is the main reason you limit your food intake?

Yeah, I mean... I think I kind of just answered that, right? Like I said a second ago, yeah, it probably is the main reason. I don't want the scale to go up, so I keep my food intake low. That's pretty much what drives it.
Do you think your weight is low even when others tell you it is?

Not really. I mean, I know my friends and my regular doctor are worried about it, but... I honestly feel like they're overreacting. I'm still showing up to my painting jobs every day and getting all my work done just fine. If it was actually a serious problem, I wouldn't be able to work like I do. So, yeah, I don't really see it the way they do.
Do you think your weight is low when you see yourself in the mirror, or do you see yourself as being at a normal weight?

I don't really see myself as being at a low weight when I look in the mirror. It's more like... I'm just looking for specific things. When I catch myself in the mirror, or if I see a photo of myself standing next to one of my murals, I'm mostly just checking my stomach and my face. I kind of judge how the whole day is going to go based on whether they look sharp and defined enough. If they don't, I just feel like I need to work harder at it. So, no, I don't look in the mirror and think I'm too thin.
Do you think you would still try to lose weight or maintain your current weight even if you were told by a doctor that your weight is healthy?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess if a doctor told me my weight was healthy right now, I'd probably still just want to maintain it where it is. Like I said, I'm comfortable with my routine and how I look when I check the mirror. So yeah, I don't really know if a doctor saying it's healthy would change what I do. I'd probably just keep doing what I'm doing.
